selection_reasoning: These four tasks form a coherent multi-hop sequence themed around a village blacksmith/workshop scenario. The player must first locate a stone_brick_slab structure (workshop area), which leads them to find the damaged_anvil (typically found in blacksmith areas). Finding the damaged anvil area reveals white_concrete_powder nearby that must be mined (gathering resources). Finally, with awareness of the area and having gathered materials, the player can locate and trade with a villager for an iron helmet. The dependency chain creates a natural exploration flow: find workshop → find anvil → mine materials → trade with villager.

White_concrete_powder is stored near the stone_brick_slab workshop; finding the slab area reveals the powder location

milestones.description: Uses position_near_with_facing because this is a 'find/locate' task. The stone brick slab floor spans spawn-relative coordinates (1,0,2) to (7,0,7). Target is set to the center of the slab floor at (4,0,5). Player must navigate near it (within 16 blocks) and face toward it (within 60 degrees). The slab floor is the workshop platform the player must discover first.

Uses position_near_with_facing because this is a 'find/locate' task. The damaged anvil is placed at spawn-relative (3,1,4) on the near side of the workshop. Player must navigate close enough to see it and face toward it. Max distance 16 and facing tolerance 60 degrees models 'player can see the anvil'.

Uses inventory_has because mining white concrete powder drops itself as an item that goes into the player's inventory. The player does NOT start with any white_concrete_powder in inventory, so having at least 1 confirms they mined it. This is the preferred rule type for mine tasks.

Uses inventory_has because trading with the armorer villager produces an iron helmet that goes into the player's inventory. The player does NOT start with any iron_helmet, so having at least 1 confirms the trade was completed successfully. This is the preferred rule type for trade/obtain tasks.

scene_description: A compact blacksmith workshop with oak log pillars, oak plank roof, and a stone brick slab floor. A damaged anvil sits on the near side of the workshop floor. The back section contains an armorer villager (level 5, NoAI) who is physically blocked behind a 2-block-high wall of white concrete powder. The player must find the workshop (stone brick slab), locate the damaged anvil, mine through the concrete powder barrier (using the provided diamond shovel), and then trade with the now-accessible armorer for an iron helmet.
task_text: Explore the blacksmith workshop ahead. Find the stone brick slab platform, locate the damaged anvil on it, mine through the white concrete powder wall blocking the back of the workshop, then trade with the armorer villager behind it for an iron helmet.
design_notes: Workshop at ~1-7, ~0, ~2-7. Stone brick slab floor is the base platform. Damaged anvil at ~3,~1,~4 (near side, visible upon entering). Armorer villager at ~5,~1,~6 (far side, behind barrier). White concrete powder barrier: 3-wide, 2-high wall at z=5 (from ~4 to ~6 at y=1 and y=2), plus side blocks at ~4,~1,~6 and ~6,~1,~6 to prevent going around. The barrier genuinely blocks player access to the villager — must mine at least 2 blocks (1-wide, 2-high gap) to reach the villager. Diamond shovel provided as optimal tool for concrete powder. 64 emeralds for trading (only 5 needed).
